fields.place: South India; Śrī Raṅgam (commander of the temple)
fields.works: Compiled the Ālvārs' hymns (the four volumes of the Prabandha, «Tamil Veda»); Nyāya-tattva; Yoga-rahasya
fields.notes: First ācārya of the Śrī Vaiṣṇava (Viśiṣṭādvaita) tradition, link between the Ālvārs and the ācāryas; collected the Ālvārs' Tamil hymns (Prabandha), still sung at Śrī Raṅgam. Grandfather of Yāmunācārya (#1781) through his son Īśvaramuni; took sannyāsa after his son's death.

Did bhajana on the north bank of Govinda-kuṇḍa when Manohara dāsa Paṇḍita Bābājī (#1849) came to live there. During a plague in Vṛndāvana the messenger of death came for him but could not take him while he chanted; Manohara dāsa explained that his life had been lengthened by the holy name.

fields.name: Yaśovanta dāsa (Pañcasakhā)
fields.aka: Yaśobanta Dāsa, Yasobanta Dāsa, Svarūpa Tīrtha, Suvāhera
fields.works: Prema-bhakti-brahma-gītā; other books on Śrī Caitanya's teaching
fields.notes: One of the Oṛiyā Pañcasakhās, son of Jagu Mallik and Rekhā Devī. Told by the Lord in a vision to take initiation from Śrī Caitanya, who initiated him at Purī, named him Svarūpa Tīrtha / Suvāhera (Īśvara dāsa). Sang in the saṅkīrtana, also at King Pratāparudra's festival at Cuttack (Caurāsī Ājñā). Wrote the Prema-bhakti-brahma-gītā. (The guru field said «Svarūpa Tīrth»: that was the name the Lord gave him.)
